old: May heaven send you home safely before you meet him when he comes,
new: May heaven send you home quietly first, so that you won’t meet him on the day he comes,
reason: Butler: “may heaven send you home quietly first that you may not meet with him in the day of his coming” — the draft’s “before you meet him” turns Odysseus’s wish that Amphinomus not meet him at all into a presupposed meeting (negation lost in the warning the paragraph exists to give), and “safely” replaces “quietly”.
Butler: “the importunity of this insatiable tramp” — “insatiable” (his unfillable greed, cf. ¶0 “incorrigible glutton”) is a different quality from “insufferable”.

old: you appear to be a decent person
new: you appear to be a man of some standing
reason: Butler: “you appear to be a considerable person” — a person of consequence/standing, not a morally decent one.
Butler: “I wish they might all be as limp as Irus is over yonder” — the concrete physical image (followed by the lolling head) is generalized to “helpless”.

Butler: “a large and lovely dress most exquisitely embroidered. It had twelve beautifully made brooch pins” — the draft drops “most exquisitely” and, after the ¶27 repair, prints “beautifully” twice in one sentence where Butler has two different words.

old: stop your jokes about my belly
new: stop your taunts about my belly
reason: Butler: “would cease your gibes about my belly” — “jokes” softens the insult; the same Butler word at ¶34 (“set Eurymachus … on to gibe at him”) is rendered “mock”.

old: the servants forced him forward and brought him
new: the servants forcibly tucked up his clothes for him and brought him
reason: Butler: “the servants girded him by force, and brought him” — the girding (the parallel to Odysseus girding his rags in ¶8, rendered “tucked his old rags around his waist”) is dropped.
